gaps.sentence: 'We'll be arriving on the red-eye,' they said. They said they ___ on the red-eye.
gaps.explanation: 'Will be arriving' backshifts to 'would be arriving'.

gaps.sentence: 'Well done, you've passed!' the examiner said. The examiner ___ me on passing.
'I've already spoken to the insurers,' he reminded me. He reminded me that he ___ spoken to the insurers.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect: had already spoken.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.

gaps.sentence: 'When does the library open?' she asked. She asked ___ the library opened.
gaps.explanation: The original question word 'when' is kept in the reported clause.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you finished the report?' the boss asked. The boss asked ___ finished the report.
gaps.hint: present perfect → past perfect in a yes/no question
gaps.explanation: Have you finished → whether/if I had finished; statement word order throughout.

gaps.sentence: 'We'd already booked when you called,' they said. They said they ___ already booked when I called.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect stays past perfect; only the pronoun you → I shifts.

gaps.sentence: 'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.
